title: Unipotent part and torus quotient of a smooth connected solvable group over a perfect field
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field]. All group schemes below are affine group schemes [def-sc-group-scheme] of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] over $k$, and all subgroup schemes are closed [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup]. Smoothness is as in [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], and connectedness as in [def-weil-connected-scheme]; geometrically connected means connected after extension to an algebraic closure $\bar k$ of $k$. A group scheme is solvable if it has a finite descending series of closed subgroup schemes, each normal in its predecessor, with commutative group-scheme quotients. A torus is a group scheme becoming $(\mathbf G_m)^d$ over $\bar k$ for some integer $d\geq0$, where $\mathbf G_m$ is as in [def-sc-gm-ga]. A smooth affine group is unipotent if in a faithful finite-dimensional matrix representation all its geometric points are unipotent matrices, meaning $(u-I)^N=0$ for some $N\geq1$. Assume $k$ is perfect, meaning that every algebraic extension of $k$ is separable. Let $H$ be smooth, connected and solvable. There is a smooth connected normal unipotent subgroup $H_u\subseteq H$ such that the fppf quotient $H/H_u$ is a torus. The subgroup $H_u$ contains every smooth unipotent subgroup of $H$, and its formation commutes with field extension; it is preserved by every automorphism after every field extension. If $H$ is a normal subgroup of a smooth group scheme $G$, then $H_u$ is normal in $G$. The fppf quotient is the sheafification of $A\mapsto H(A)/H_u(A)$ for faithfully flat finitely presented coverings of commutative $k$-algebras.

source.place: Theorem 16.33(a)--(c), printed pp.335--336; Proposition 1.90, printed p.33, for normality of a weakly characteristic subgroup of a normal subgroup in a smooth group; geometric-point interpretation of unipotence in Corollary 14.12 and Section 14(c), printed pp.283, 286--287.

proof.text: Put $F=\bar k$. By [lem-sfb-solvable-normal-subgroup-products], $H_F$ is smooth, connected and solvable. Apply [lem-sfb-lie-kolchin-triangular-embedding] to obtain $H_F\hookrightarrow B_n$, and put $V=H_F\cap U_n$. By [lem-sfb-triangular-diagonal-kernel], $V$ is smooth, connected, normal and unipotent, and $D=H_F/V$ is a smooth connected closed subgroup of $(\mathbf G_m)^n$. The smooth-connected clause of [lem-sfb-multiplicative-type-largest-subtorus] makes $D$ a torus.

source.place: Theorem 16.33 proof, through Theorem 16.30, Proposition 16.2 and Note 16.10, printed pp.325–326,334–336.

proof.text: The same kernel characterization works over any field: if $N\triangleleft J$ is unipotent and $J/N$ is of multiplicative type, every unipotent subgroup $W\subseteq J$ maps trivially to $J/N$ by [lem-sfb-unipotent-to-multiplicative-trivial]. The scheme-theoretic kernel assertion of [lem-sfb-affine-normal-quotient-geometry] then gives $W\subseteq N$. For two such kernels, apply this argument in both directions; they are equal as subgroup schemes. In particular $V$ from step 1 is independent of the chosen triangular representation.

source.place: Theorem 16.6 proof, first paragraph, and Note 16.8, printed p.326.

proof.text: Since $k$ is perfect, $F/k$ is Galois. For every $\sigma\in\operatorname{Gal}(F/k)$ the conjugate $\sigma(V)$ is again normal and unipotent in $H_F$ with torus quotient: scalar transport carries the subgroup, quotient and displayed matrix properties to their $\sigma$-transforms. Step 2 forces $\sigma(V)=V$. Thus its defining ideal is Galois-stable. Apply [lem-sfb-galois-descent-affine-subgroups] to obtain $H_u\subseteq H$ with $(H_u)_F=V$, and to descend normality. Smoothness descends by [lem-trf-smooth-fpqc-base-descent], using the flat quasi-compact surjection $\operatorname{Spec}F\to\operatorname{Spec}k$. Connectedness descends because a disconnection of $H_u$ into two nonempty clopen subsets would pull back to one of $V$. Unipotence is detected after extension by [lem-sfb-unipotent-to-multiplicative-trivial]. By [lem-sfb-affine-normal-quotient-geometry], the fppf quotient $Q=H/H_u$ is represented and $Q_F=H_F/V=D$. Consequently $Q$ becomes a product of copies of $\mathbf G_m$ over $F$, exactly the definition of a $k$-torus.

source.place: Theorem 16.6 proof of (a)⇒(b), Section 1.54(b), Notes 16.8–16.10 and Theorem 16.33, printed pp.21–22,326,335–336.

proof.text: Let $K/k$ be any field extension, including an imperfect transcendental extension. The base-changed subgroup $(H_u)_K$ is normal, smooth and connected by [lem-sfb-solvable-normal-subgroup-products], and unipotent by [lem-sfb-unipotent-to-multiplicative-trivial]. By [lem-sfb-affine-normal-quotient-geometry] its quotient is $Q_K$, a group of multiplicative type by the scalar-extension assertion of [lem-sfb-unipotent-to-multiplicative-trivial]. Apply step 2 over $K$: $(H_u)_K$ contains every smooth unipotent subgroup of $H_K$ and is the unique normal unipotent kernel with multiplicative-type quotient. This proves field-extension compatibility without assuming $K$ perfect. Taking $K=k$ proves the requested maximality as well.

For an automorphism $a$ of $H_K$, the subgroup $a((H_u)_K)$ is smooth, connected and unipotent (the faithful representation can be precomposed with $a^{-1}$), normal in $H_K$, and has quotient isomorphic to $Q_K$. Both it and $(H_u)_K$ therefore satisfy the characterization of step 2, so they are equal. Equivalently, maximality in step 4 applied to $a$ and $a^{-1}$ gives the two subgroup inclusions. This is invariance under automorphisms after every field extension; it makes no claim of invariance under automorphisms over arbitrary nonreduced base algebras.

source.place: Note 16.8, printed p.326, and Definition 1.89, printed p.33.

proof.text: Finally assume $H\triangleleft G$ with $G$ smooth. For every $g\in G(F)$, conjugation restricts to an automorphism of $H_F$, since normality holds after scalar extension. Step 5 gives $\operatorname{Int}(g)((H_u)_F)=(H_u)_F$ as subgroup schemes. The criterion [lem-sfb-smooth-ambient-normality-geometric] applies to the closed subgroup $H_u\subseteq G$ and yields $H_u\triangleleft G$. The ambient smoothness hypothesis is exactly the one required by that criterion.

proof_origin.place: Theorem 16.33(a)–(c), using the proof of Theorem 16.6, Notes 16.8–16.10 and Proposition 1.90. Algebraic-closure descent spells out the same separable-descent argument without choosing a finite splitting extension.

split_report.summary: Read Milne Theorem 16.33 and its prerequisites. Construct the diagonal kernel after Lie–Kolchin, prove uniqueness by vanishing of maps to multiplicative type, descend its Galois-stable ideal, and deduce arbitrary field-extension compatibility, weak characteristicness and normality in a smooth ambient group. Five statement-only auxiliary nodes; reuse four existing group-scheme tools and the existing Mathlib fpqc-smooth-descent leaf. Only statement change is removal of inherited doubled TeX backslashes, with no mathematical change.

lean.statement: theorem perfect_solvable_unipotent_torus {k : Type u} [Field k] [PerfectField k] (H : Grp (Over (Spec (.of k)))) (hH : IsAlgebraic H) (hsm : Smooth H.X.hom) (hc : ConnectedSpace H.X.left) (hs : IsSolvable H) : ∃ (U : Grp (Over (Spec (.of k)))) (i : U ⟶ H) (Q : Grp (Over (Spec (.of k)))) (q : H ⟶ Q), IsAlgebraic U ∧ Smooth U.X.hom ∧ ConnectedSpace U.X.left ∧ IsUnipotent U ∧ IsClosedSubgroupScheme i.hom.hom ∧ IsNormalSubgroupScheme i.hom.hom ∧ IsAlgebraic Q ∧ IsTorus Q ∧ IsFppfQuotient i.hom.hom q ∧ (∀ (W : Grp (Over (Spec (.of k)))) (j : W ⟶ H), IsAlgebraic W → IsUnipotent W → IsClosedSubgroupScheme j.hom.hom → ∃ l : W ⟶ U, l ≫ i = j) ∧ (∀ (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K], IsUnipotent ((extend K).obj U) ∧ ConnectedSpace ((extend K).obj U).X.left ∧ IsClosedSubgroupScheme ((extend K).map i).hom.hom ∧ IsNormalSubgroupScheme ((extend K).map i).hom.hom ∧ IsTorus ((extend K).obj Q) ∧ IsFppfQuotient ((extend K).map i).hom.hom ((extend K).map q) ∧ (∀ (W : Grp (Over (Spec (.of K)))) (j : W ⟶ (extend K).obj H), IsAlgebraic W → IsUnipotent W → IsClosedSubgroupScheme j.hom.hom → ∃ l : W ⟶ (extend K).obj U, l ≫ (extend K).map i = j) ∧ (∀ a : (extend K).obj H ≅ (extend K).obj H, ∃ b : (extend K).obj U ≅ (extend K).obj U, b.hom ≫ (extend K).map i = (extend K).map i ≫ a.hom)) ∧ (∀ (G : Grp (Over (Spec (.of k)))) (j : H ⟶ G), IsAlgebraic G → Smooth G.X.hom → IsClosedSubgroupScheme j.hom.hom → IsNormalSubgroupScheme j.hom.hom → IsNormalSubgroupScheme (i ≫ j).hom.hom)
